conventions.verified: Plain text facts/numbers were read on a fetched source page listed in that sport's sources.
conventions.[unverified]: Seen only in search-result snippets or secondary summaries, not confirmed on a fetched page. Do not ship as a hard rule without checking.
conventions.[derived]: Somax design choice built from the sourced facts (interpolation, caps, rounding). Not a claim made by any source. Tune with real user data.

globalRules.taper: Bosquet et al. 2007 meta-analysis (MSSE 39(8):1358-65), abstract as quoted in search results: best taper is ~2 weeks, volume cut 41-60% in a progressive/exponential way, intensity and frequency kept. [unverified - PubMed page blocked fetch; numbers consistent across 2+ secondary results]
globalRules.intensityDistribution: Polarized (~75-80% low / ~5% threshold / ~15-20% high) is a description of elite training from Seiler's work. In Stoggl & Sperlich 2014 (9 weeks, well-trained athletes) the polarized group (68/6/26) improved VO2peak 11.7% vs no significant change for threshold and high-volume groups. Somax default: most minutes easy, 1-2 hard sessions/week. [derived]
globalRules.recoveryWeeks: Stoggl & Sperlich 2014 used 3-week blocks: 2 loading weeks + 1 recovery week. FitnessVolt HYROX plan: week 4 deload at ~60% volume. Somax default: every 3rd week (if age 40+ or beginner) or 4th week at ~60-70% volume, intensity kept short. [derived]
globalRules.volumeRampLimits: Buist 2008 (novice runners, per secondary summaries) found a 10%/week rule did not reduce injury vs ~24%/week [unverified]. CTS (trainright.com) recommends capping growth of the single longest session at ~10% per month vs the previous 30 days for running, and judging weekly volume by 24-48 h recovery. Somax default: cap the longest session jump per week (sport-specific below); if user reports soreness/stiffness lasting >48 h, repeat the week. [derived]
globalRules.gapEngine: [derived] weeksNeeded = ceil(gap / expectedWeeklyRate(level)) + taperWeeks. Clamp to [minWeeks, maxWeeks]. If weeksNeeded > maxWeeks, split into milestone blocks (each block ends with a retest and a recalculated next target); the user sees block 1 target + the long-term target.

benchmarks.label: FTP (20-minute test)
benchmarks.howToTest: Thorough warm-up (optional hard 5-min effort then easy spinning [unverified]). Ride one self-paced 20-minute time trial at the highest power you can hold. Indoors use resistance/slope mode, not ERG. FTP = 0.95 x 20-min average power. Note: the 0.95 factor fits only ~50-60% of riders (range seen 86-96%).

benchmarks.label: FTP (ramp test)
benchmarks.howToTest: After a warm-up, start at 100 W and add 20 W every minute until you cannot continue (ERG mode on a smart trainer). Without an app, FTP = 0.75 x power of the last completed 1-minute stage.

benchmarks.label: FTP (2 x 8-minute test)
benchmarks.howToTest: After a warm-up, ride two 8-minute time trials separated by 10 minutes easy spinning. FTP = 0.90 x the higher of the two averages (CTS method).

benchmarks.label: Body weight (for W/kg)
benchmarks.howToTest: Morning weight. Used only to compute W/kg for level placement.

benchmarks.label: Longest comfortable ride in last 4 weeks
benchmarks.howToTest: Distance of the longest ride completed at easy/conversational effort in the last 4 weeks. Used for distance goals and for riders without a power meter. [derived]

benchmarks.label: Longest comfortable ride (time)
benchmarks.howToTest: Same as above in minutes; use if the user rides indoors. [derived]

coggan.name: VO2max

sweetSpot.notes: TrainerRoad and TrainingPeaks both define it as 88-94% FTP; TrainerRoad's own table uses Tempo 76-87, Sweet Spot 88-94, Threshold 95-105.

zoneModel.heartRateFallback: Coggan HR column (% of threshold HR): Z1 <68, Z2 69-83, Z3 84-94, Z4 95-105, Z5 >106. Use only if no power meter.
zoneModel.rpeFallback: Cycling UK talk test: easy = can hold a conversation; steady = can talk in short sentences; harder efforts = Z4-ish. [derived mapping: easy=Z1-2, steady=Z3, harder=Z4]
zoneModel.formula: targetWatts = round(FTP x pct / 100). Example FTP 200 W: Z2 = 112-150 W; sweet spot = 176-188 W; threshold = 182-210 W.

ftp.observed: TrainerRoad data on riders following plans: ~5% gain in 20-min power after 2 months, ~9% after 4 months, ~10% by summer. Riders doing 3 hard days/week (avg ~5 h/week) improved 5-60 min power more than those doing 2.
ftp.research: Stoggl & Sperlich 2014: polarized training +5.1% peak power and +8.1% power at 4 mmol in 9 weeks (well-trained athletes).
ftp.expectedWeeklyRate: [derived] beginner/untrained 1.0%/wk for first 8 weeks then 0.5%; novice 0.7%/wk; intermediate 0.5%/wk; advanced 0.25%/wk. Rates halve after week 16. (TrainerRoad average ~0.6%/wk over first 8 weeks; beginners assumed faster - unverified.)

distance.observed: Cycling UK 10-week plan takes the long ride from 15-25 km (week 1) to 90-100 km (week 9), i.e. roughly +10 km per week, then a 2-ride taper week.
distance.expectedWeeklyRate: [derived] long ride +10 km/week (or +15 min) for beginners/novices; +15 km/week if longest_ride_km >= 60; never more than +30% in one week.

planLengthRule.ftpGoal: [derived] gapPct = (targetFTP - currentFTP)/currentFTP x 100. weeks = ceil(gapPct / expectedWeeklyRate) + 1 (test week). Clamp min 6 (shortest retest interval per CTS is ~6 weeks), max 16. If gapPct > maxSingleBlockGain or weeks > 16, split into blocks of 8-12 weeks, each ending with an FTP retest and recalculated zones.
planLengthRule.distanceGoal: [derived] weeks = ceil((targetKm - longestRideKm) / weeklyLongRideIncrease) + 1 taper week. Clamp min 4, max 16. Peak long ride should reach 90-100% of target 1-2 weeks before the event (Cycling UK peaks at 90-100 km for a 100 km ride in week 9 of 10). If > 16 weeks, milestone block 1 target = longest + 16 x increase.
planLengthRule.retest: FTP retest no sooner than ~6 weeks; ideally after a recovery week (CTS).

volumeModel.start: British Cycling beginner plan (25 weeks to a 60-mile/100 km sportive): 3-7.5 h/week, 3 rides/week (1 midweek, 2 weekend) + optional cross-training. Cycling UK 100 km plan: 3-4 rides/week, 2-3 rest days/week.
volumeModel.startRule: [derived] week-1 weekly time = clamp(1.5 x longest_ride_min, 90, 300) min, spread over chosen days with the long ride ~40% of weekly time.
volumeModel.progression: [derived] weekly time +5-10%, long ride per improvementModel.distance; hard sessions progress by interval duration first (e.g. 3x5 -> 4x5 -> 2x10 min as in Cycling UK), then by intensity.
volumeModel.recoveryWeeks: [derived] every 3rd (beginner/40+) or 4th week at 60-70% of previous week's volume, keep one short quality session. Basis: Stoggl & Sperlich 2+1 block structure.
volumeModel.taper: Event goals: final 1-2 weeks, volume down ~40-60%, keep intensity and frequency (Bosquet, unverified). Cycling UK final week: two short easy rides (60 and 45 min). FTP goals: replace taper with 4-5 easy days before the retest.
volumeModel.intensityMix: [derived] beginners: 0-1 hard session/week for first 4 weeks (Cycling UK adds harder efforts from week 5); later 1-2. Intermediate+: 2 (3 only if >=5 days and recovering well, per TrainerRoad data).

2: Midweek: quality ride (sweet spot / harder efforts) 45-60 min
3: Weekend: long ride (steady section in middle once base built)
6: As 5 days + one extra easy endurance ride; never 3 hard days in a row [derived]
weekStructure.notes: Pattern from Cycling UK (Tue intervals, Thu easy, weekend long) and British Cycling (1 midweek + 2 weekend). Separate hard days by >=1 easy/rest day. [derived]

benchmarks.label: Critical Swim Speed (CSS)
benchmarks.howToTest: Warm up thoroughly. Swim 400m all-out but evenly paced; recover 5-10 min with easy swimming; swim 200m all-out; cool down. CSS (s/100m) = (T400 - T200) / 2. The 200 must be faster per 100m than the 400 or the result is invalid. Test in the pool length you usually train in.

benchmarks.label: 400m time trial
benchmarks.howToTest: First half of the CSS test. Also the direct benchmark for goals like '400m under 8:00'.

benchmarks.label: 100m time
benchmarks.howToTest: After warm-up, one hard but controlled 100m freestyle. Quick benchmark for users who cannot yet swim 400m. [derived]

benchmarks.label: Longest continuous swim
benchmarks.howToTest: Swim easy, any stroke allowed but note stroke, without stopping or holding the wall; record metres completed (25m pool = count lengths x 25). [derived]

levelPlacement.rule: [derived] by longest_continuous: <100m -> 'learn-to-swim' (refer to adult lessons, Swim England Adult Swimming Framework; do not run a CSS test); 100-399m -> beginner (no CSS test yet; use time_100 + RPE); 400-999m -> novice (CSS test valid); >=1000m -> intermediate; intermediate with CSS faster than 1:40/100m -> advanced [unverified cut-off].
supportingFacts: Triathlete 8-week sprint plan requires being able to swim 100 yards nonstop; by week 6 it prescribes 1000 nonstop.
Swim England's adult framework has 4 progressive stages; a provider using it sets 100m continuous as the entry-level goal [unverified - search snippet].
Swim England fitness plan is 20 sessions starting at ~300m per session with kick/float work (only session 1 is public).

zoneModel.noCssFallback: Triathlete RPE zones: Z1 easy rhythmic breathing; Z2 slightly deeper, can still talk; Z3 moderate 'feel-good fast'; Z4 hard, ~15-min all-out swim pace; Z5 all-out 1-5 min.
zoneModel.pacingTool: Pace per length = CSS/100 x pool length (e.g. 2:00/100 in 25m pool = 30 s per length; beep per length on a Tempo Trainer).
zoneModel.formula: zonePace(s/100m) = CSS + offset. Example CSS 2:00 -> steady 2:06, easy 2:08-2:10.

pace.observed: Swim Smooth: beginners often gain 5-10 s/100m in CSS; well-trained swimmers 1-2 s/100m is significant; improving CSS by 3-4 s/100m is a good target. Search snippet claims 4-10 s/100m over 8 weeks of CSS training [unverified].
pace.expectedWeeklyRate: [derived] beginner/novice 0.75 s/100m per week (=~6 s over 8 weeks); intermediate 0.4 s/wk; advanced 0.15 s/wk.
pace.inSessionAdjust: Swim Smooth: if a CSS session was too easy, lower the target pace (one reply suggests 3 s steps for beginners; their GURU 'strong' tweak is <1 s/100m); if too hard, slow it 3-5 s/100m and work back down.

distance.observed: Triathlete plan moves a swimmer who can do 100 yds nonstop to 1000 nonstop in 6 weeks with 2 swims/week, using short reps with rest (16x25, 10x50, 8x75, 4x100, 2x200 + 4x100, 500 + 5x100, then 1000). Swim Serpentine: break a target distance into shorter reps with short rests (e.g. 1000m as 10x100), and periodically do a timed non-stop swim.
distance.expectedWeeklyRate: [derived] longest continuous +50% per week while under 400m, then +100-150m/week to 1000m, then +200m/week. Main set total should reach ~target distance before the continuous attempt.

planLengthRule.paceGoal: [derived] Convert target to per-100m pace (e.g. 400m in 8:00 = 2:00/100). Use time_400 pace (not CSS) for 400m goals: gap = current400pace - target400pace. weeks = ceil(gap / expectedWeeklyRate) + 1 (test week). Clamp min 4, max 12. If >12, milestone block 1 = current - 12 x rate; retest CSS every 4-6 weeks (Swim Smooth; their newer blog says retest less often and tweak instead).
planLengthRule.distanceGoal: [derived] Simulate the weekly increase schedule above from longest_continuous to target; weeks = steps + 1. Clamp min 3, max 12. Learn-to-swim users (<100m) get a pre-plan: adult lessons recommendation + kick/float technique block before any distance plan.
planLengthRule.combinedGoal: [derived] If a pace goal is set but longest_continuous < goal distance, run the distance plan first, then the pace plan.

volumeModel.start: [derived] beginner: 2 sessions/week, ~300-600m (Swim England session 1 ~300m; Triathlete week 1 16x25 and 10x50). Novice: 2-3 sessions, 1000-1800m. Intermediate: 3+ sessions, 2000m+ (Swim Smooth suggests building toward ~2000 yds/session before long CSS efforts).
volumeModel.sessionStructure: Warm-up -> main set -> contrast set (kick/drills) -> warm-down (Swim Serpentine / London Marathon Events).
volumeModel.progression: [derived] session volume +10-15%/week; within CSS sets add reps (3 -> 4 x 100) or lengthen the final rep (200 -> 300 -> 400, Goldilocks Baby->Mama->Papa) before speeding up.
volumeModel.recoveryWeeks: [derived] every 4th week -25-35% volume, keep one CSS set.
volumeModel.taper: Event goals: last week shorter sessions, a few short fast reps (Triathlete week 8: 200 easy + 8x50 alternating hard/easy). Bosquet 2-week taper rule for >=10-week plans [unverified].

1: Mixed: technique warm-up + CSS/pace set or distance-building set
2: Session A: distance/aerobic (reps with short rest, steady)
Session B: technique + pace (CSS or Z3-4 short reps)
3: Endurance/open-water or long continuous session (Swim Smooth 3-session week: technique, open water skills, CSS)
4: As 3 + an extra easy aerobic/drill session [derived]

raceFormat.structure: 8 x (1 km run + 1 station); 8 km running total. Transitions (Roxzone) count toward finish time.
raceFormat.conflicts: FitnessVolt's plan lists wall balls 9 kg / 6 kg (likely Pro or older standard) - use hyrox.com Open values. hyrox.com 'best preparation' page mentions a 125 kg sled - season/division differences; confirm per event. Pro division uses heavier loads.

benchmarks.label: 5 km run time
benchmarks.howToTest: Best-effort 5 km after warm-up. Prerequisite for the standard 8-week plan is running 5 km comfortably (FitnessVolt target <30 min).

benchmarks.label: 1 km run time (fresh)
benchmarks.howToTest: Best-effort 1 km after warm-up. [derived]

benchmarks.label: 1000 m SkiErg
benchmarks.howToTest: Controlled hard effort, steady rhythm. [derived]

benchmarks.label: 1000 m row
benchmarks.howToTest: Controlled hard effort. [derived]

benchmarks.label: Half simulation
benchmarks.howToTest: 4 x (1 km run + station 1-4 or 5-8) at race weights or scaled; record total time and which station broke form. [derived from FitnessVolt simulation format]

benchmarks.label: Max unbroken wall balls
benchmarks.howToTest: Open-division ball, standard depth and target; stop at first no-rep. [derived]

levelPlacement.rule: [derived] Cannot run 5 km continuously -> 'foundation' (run-building block first, see planLengthRule). 5 km in >=30 min or no gym equipment experience -> beginner. 5 km <30 min + can complete all stations at Open weight (scaled reps OK) -> novice. Has finished a HYROX or completes full simulation -> intermediate. Sub-25 min 5 km and full simulation near goal time -> advanced.
levelPlacement.prerequisitesFitnessVolt: Run 5 km without stopping (target <30 min); basic gym experience (rower, squat/lunge mechanics); SkiErg or rower access; sled or sandbag substitute; ~3-3.5 h/week in build weeks.

zoneModel.run: FitnessVolt Day 1 intervals: 1 km at target race pace, ~80% effort, reaching 85-90% HRmax; 60-90 s rest between sets. Easy runs conversational (Z2). [derived for easy]
zoneModel.racePace: [derived] targetRunPace = (goalTime - estimatedStationTime - roxzoneAllowance) / 8 per km; estimate stations from benchmark ergs + simulation splits.
zoneModel.pacing: hyrox.com: do not start too fast; treat like a half marathon/Olympic triathlon effort and control heart rate. Red Bull: pace the sled push with short pauses; rowing too hard saves seconds but costs more later.
zoneModel.strength: Station strength work in quality sets with full recovery, not circuits (FitnessVolt).

improvementModel.observed: No published improvement-rate data found for HYROX. [unverified]
improvementModel.approach: [derived] Split goal-time gap into running gap and station gap from the half simulation. Running improves per running playbook rates; station time improves fastest early (technique + standards) - assume 10-15% station-time drop over first 8 weeks for beginners [unverified assumption].

planLengthRule.rule: Default 8 weeks at 3 days/week for users meeting prerequisites (FitnessVolt). [derived] Foundation users (cannot run 5 km): prepend 4-8 weeks of run-building + station technique. Advanced users with a time goal: 10-12 weeks with two 4-week build blocks. Clamp min 6, max 16.
planLengthRule.milestones: Week 3: 4 km + 4 stations; week 6: full 8 km + 8 stations simulation (FitnessVolt). [derived] Each simulation result recalculates race pace.

volumeModel.start: FitnessVolt 3-day plan: ~3-3.5 h/week in build weeks. Red Bull (HYROX Elite athlete advice): 3 sessions/week can cover endurance, strength and race-specific fitness [unverified - snippet]. Some pros train 6 days/week [unverified - snippet].
volumeModel.progression: FitnessVolt: run intervals 3x1 km -> 6x1 km; simulation 2 km + 2 stations -> 8 km + 8 stations by week 6; station work from technique to full weights.
volumeModel.recoveryWeeks: FitnessVolt week 4 deload at ~60% volume (easy runs, technique/mobility, short easy simulation).
volumeModel.taper: FitnessVolt week 8: 3 x 1 km easy + light erg, light station rehearsal, race day. Week 7 'peak' at race effort (6 km + 6 stations).

5: 4-day pattern + compromised-running session (stations straight into short runs) [derived]
6: 5-day pattern + extra easy run or mobility; keep 1 rest day [derived]
weekStructure.notes: hyrox.com: practise running on fatigued legs and arms; learn official movement standards.

safety: hyrox.com: learn the official movement standards to avoid poor form and injury; consider a certified coach.
hyrox.com: rest, eat and hydrate through training and race build-up.
Red Bull: pace the sled push (short pauses) - going all-out ruins the following run; resting on the sled pull is allowed but leaving the lane area is penalised.
[derived] Scale loads (not just reps) for beginners: start stations at ~50-70% of race weight and build to race weight by week 5.
[derived] Users who cannot run 5 km continuously start with a run-building block before race-specific work.
